    const x2 = dstR.left - flowRect.left;

    path.setAttribute('stroke', '#c05030');
    path.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.5');
    path.setAttribute('marker-end', 'url(#ar)');

-- Types
  type PartId    = Text
  type Component = Text
  type Tokens    = Int

  data PartWithContext =
    { partId       :: PartId
    , messageIndex :: Int
    , role         :: Text       -- "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool"
    , partType     :: Text       -- "text" | "reasoning" | "tool-call" | "tool-result" | "image" | "file"
    , content      :: Value      -- text string, or structured object, or placeholder
    }


  -- COMPONENT MAPPING
  -- Assigns every message part to one of the identified components.
  -- Parts are extracted with context, batched, and sent to AI in parallel.
  -- Results are merged into a single mapping. Unmapped parts get "other".


  -- Step 1: Strip large content
  -- Same stripping as identification: images → "[IMAGE_STRIPPED]",
  -- files → "[FILE_DATA_STRIPPED]", tool I/O → truncated to 200 chars.
  -- Mapping operates on the stripped conversation, not the original.


  -- Step 2: Extract parts with context
  -- Flatten every part from every message into a list, enriching each
  -- with its message position and role so the AI understands discourse flow.

  extractPartsWithContext :: Conversation -> [PartWithContext]
    -- for each message at index i:
    --   for each part in message.parts:
    --     content = case part.type of
    --       "text"        -> part.text
    --       "reasoning"   -> part.text
    --       "tool-call"   -> { toolName: part.toolName, input: part.input }
    --       "tool-result" -> { toolName: part.toolName, output: part.output }
    --       "image"       -> "[IMAGE]"
    --       "file"        -> "[FILE]"
    --     emit { partId: part.id, messageIndex: i, role: message.role,
    --            partType: part.type, content }


  -- Step 3: Batch
  -- Split the flat list of parts into chunks of 20.
  -- The last batch may have fewer than 20 parts.

  batchSize = 20

  batch :: [PartWithContext] -> [[PartWithContext]]
    -- chunks of batchSize from the parts list
    -- e.g. 45 parts → [20, 20, 5]


  -- Step 4: Map each batch (AI call)
  -- Each batch is sent to the AI with the list of components.
  -- The AI classifies every part in the batch.

  mapPartsBatch :: [PartWithContext] -> [Component] -> Map PartId Component
    -- prompt:
    --   "given this conversation and the list of components, give me a mapping
    --    of message part ids in the conversation, to a component from the list,
    --    for all the message parts
    --    just give me a simple json object {id: component}
    --
    --    <conversation>{partsJson}</conversation>
    --    <components>{componentsJson}</components>"
    --
    -- result = generateText(model, prompt)
    --
    -- Parse response:
    --   jsonMatch = result.text.match(/\{[^]*\}/s)   -- find first JSON object
    --   if no match → return {}
    --   rawMapping = JSON.parse(jsonMatch)
    --   if not object → return {}
    --
    -- Normalize values:
    --   for each (key, value) in rawMapping:
    --     mapping[key] = value.replace("^- *", "")    -- strip leading "- "
    --   return mapping
    --
    -- On any error → return {} (empty mapping for this batch)


  -- Step 5: Process all batches in parallel and merge

  mapComponentsToIds :: [Component] -> Conversation -> Map PartId Component
    -- stripped  = stripLargeContent(conversation)
    -- allParts  = extractPartsWithContext(stripped)
    -- batches   = batch(allParts)
    -- results   = parallel(map (\b -> mapPartsBatch b components) batches)
    --               -- all batches execute concurrently via Promise.all
    -- merged    = foldl Object.assign {} results
    --               -- simple dictionary union; part IDs are unique across batches
    -- return merged


  -- Step 6: Handle unmapped parts
  -- After mapping, some parts may not appear in the merged result
  -- (AI omitted them, or a batch call failed). These get "other".
  --
  -- The "other" component is added to the component list only if needed:
  --   totalParts  = sum (map (length . parts) conversation.messages)
  --   mappedParts = length (keys merged)
  --   if mappedParts < totalParts && "other" not in components:
  --     finalComponents = components ++ ["other"]
  --
  -- In the timeline and visualization, unmapped parts are assigned to
  -- "other" at lookup time:
  --   component = mapping[partId] ?? "other"


  -- TIMELINE
  -- Built deterministically from the mapping (no AI).
  -- Accumulates token counts per component as you walk through messages.

  data ComponentTimelineSnapshot =
    { messageIndex    :: Int
    , componentTokens :: Map Component Tokens   -- cumulative per component
    , totalTokens     :: Tokens                 -- cumulative total
    }

  buildComponentTimeline :: Conversation -> Map PartId Component -> [ComponentTimelineSnapshot]
    -- First, build an index: partId → { messageIndex, tokenCount }
    --   for each message at index i:
    --     for each part:
    --       partInfo[part.id] = { messageIndex: i, tokenCount: part.token_count ?? 0 }
    --
    -- Then, for each message index from 0 to N-1:
    --   componentTokens = {}
    --   totalTokens = 0
    --   for each (partId, info) in partInfo where info.messageIndex <= current:
    --     component = mapping[partId] ?? "other"
    --     componentTokens[component] += info.tokenCount
    --     totalTokens += info.tokenCount
    --   emit { messageIndex, componentTokens, totalTokens }


  -- ORCHESTRATION
  -- componentiseConversation ties identification and mapping together.

  componentiseConversation :: Maybe Prompt -> Maybe [Component] -> Conversation
                           -> { components :: [Component]
                              , mapping    :: Map PartId Component
                              , timeline   :: [ComponentTimelineSnapshot]
                              , error      :: Maybe Text }

    -- If customComponents provided and non-empty:
    --   components = normalize(customComponents)     -- strip "- " prefixes
    -- Else:
    --   components = identifyComponents(customPrompt, conversation)
    --   if components == [] → return error
    --
    -- mapping  = mapComponentsToIds(components, conversation)
    -- add "other" to components if any parts unmapped
    -- timeline = buildComponentTimeline(conversation, mapping)
    -- return { components, mapping, timeline }


  -- Interactive iteration
  -- When the user edits the component list:
  --   1. identification is SKIPPED (custom components used)
  --   2. mapComponentsToIds reruns against the new list
  --   3. assignColors reruns
  --   4. timeline is rebuilt
  --
  -- When segmentation changes upstream:
  --   - Part IDs change (new segments get "parentId.1", "parentId.2", ...)
  --   - Both identification and mapping must rerun
  --   - Old mappings are invalidated

message.content: Explain what extract parts is doing to me.

content.text:
Based on the spec in `context-viewer-component-mapping.md`:

**Extract Parts** flattens the conversation into a list of individual parts. Each message in a conversation can have multiple parts (a text block, a tool-call, a tool-result, an image, etc.). This step walks through every message in order and pulls out each part as a standalone item, enriching it with context:

- **partId** - the part's unique ID (e.g. `p1`, `p2`)
- **messageIndex** - which message it came from (so the LLM knows the order)
- **role** - who said it (`user`, `assistant`, `tool`)
- **partType** - what kind of content (`text`, `tool-call`, `tool-result`, `image`, etc.)
- **content** - the actual text/data (already stripped)

So a conversation like:

```
Message 0 (user):   [text part]
Message 1 (asst):   [text part, tool-call part]
Message 2 (tool):   [tool-result part]
Message 3 (asst):   [text part]
```

Becomes a flat list:

```
p1  msg:0  user  text
p2  msg:1  asst  text
p3  msg:1  asst  tool-call
p4  msg:2  tool  tool-result
p5  msg:3  asst  text
```

The purpose is to get every part into a uniform shape so they can be batched (chunks of 20) and sent to the LLM for classification. Each part gets mapped to a topic independently, and the message context (index + role) helps the LLM understand where it fits in the conversation flow.

content.text:
Yes, by this point the segments *are* the message parts. 

The segmentation step (diagram 1) split large message parts into smaller chunks. So a message that originally had one big text part with ~25k tokens now has 5 smaller text parts (the segments) inside it. Those segments replaced the original part within the message.

So when Extract Parts flattens the conversation, each segment is its own part with its own ID. From the spec:

> Part IDs change (new segments get "parentId.1", "parentId.2", ...)

For example, if segmentation split part `p2` into 3 segments, the flat list would look like:

```
p1      msg:0  user  text
p2.1    msg:1  asst  text       ← segment 1
p2.2    msg:1  asst  text       ← segment 2
p2.3    msg:1  asst  text       ← segment 3
p3      msg:1  asst  tool-call
p4      msg:2  tool  tool-result
...
```

Extract Parts doesn't know or care about the segmentation - it just sees a conversation where some messages have more (smaller) parts than they used to. Each segment gets mapped to a topic independently by the LLM.

message.content: Is it each part getting mapped or each segment getting mapped?

content.text:
Each **part** gets mapped - and segments are parts. After segmentation, the conversation's parts list already contains the segments as first-class parts. There's no distinction anymore.

A message's parts array might look like:

```
parts: [
  { id: "p2.1", type: "text", text: "## Setup..." },    ← was a segment
  { id: "p2.2", type: "text", text: "## Impl..." },     ← was a segment
  { id: "p3",   type: "tool-call", toolName: "Read" },   ← was never segmented
]
```

Extract Parts flattens all of these uniformly. The mapping step maps every part ID (whether it was a segment or an original small part) to a topic. It's all just parts by this point.
